title: Yogesh Kumar v. State of U.P.
coram: Dilip B. Bhosale, C.J. and Yashwant Varma, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to Clause 6.5.
headnote: Without examining the correctness of the electricity bill, the Court disposed of the writ, holding that Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides a complete machinery for billing grievances and leaving the consumer to pursue that statutory remedy.
facts: Yogesh Kumar filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court questioning an electricity bill raised against him by the respondent licensee and seeking disposal of his representation dated 15 June 2016, which challenged the correctness of that bill. The Division Bench heard counsel for the petitioner, the State, and the licensee. Licensee counsel submitted that the Supply Code supplied a complete grievance machinery for such billing objections. The Court did not inquire into the bill itself.

holding_units.holding: Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 lays down a complete machinery for redressal of grievances questioning the correctness of an electricity bill. A writ seeking disposal of a representation against such a bill is disposed of without examining merits, leaving the consumer to institute appropriate proceedings under Clause 6.5.

not_decided.point: correctness of the electricity bill and the petitioner's objections to it
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to go into the merits of the objections.
